discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived the idea of turning a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a neutrino telescope, and over three decades he drove its realisation from AMANDA to IceCube. In 2013 IceCube reported the first evidence of a diffuse flux of high-energy neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin, at TeV-PeV energies, opening an entirely new window on the universe. This was followed by the identification of the blazar TXS 0506+056 as a neutrino source (2018), neutrinos from the active galaxy NGC 1068 (2022), and the first neutrino image of the Galactic plane (2023). Neutrinos are ideal messengers: they travel undeflected by magnetic fields and unabsorbed by matter, and so they reveal the sites of cosmic-ray acceleration. The idea is simple, but making it work was extraordinarily difficult, and Halzen's vision and persistence were decisive. The citation is sharply drawn: the discovery of cosmic neutrinos, which founded neutrino astronomy at high energies.
